text:
Priya: hi all, first-day laptop issue — got a ThinkPad from shipping, did the OOBE, logged in, then Windows installed updates and now BitLocker asked for a recovery key at boot. Intune shows the device but "BitLocker recovery key not found". stuck on boot screen with recovery code prompt.
ben-windows-it: welcome Priya — sorry about that. quick Q: was there a temporary local admin account you used during provisioning or did you sign in with the company AAD account from the start?
Priya: signed in with my company account during OOBE. no extra local admin. laptop label says company asset tag 12345-LP.
intune-bot: Intune last check-in: 2025-11-03T15:02:11Z. Device state: AzureAD Joined, BitLocker: Protection On, Recovery keys: 0 available to tenant. Pending actions: sync, push-key.
ben-windows-it: hmm — sometimes when the TPM is cleared or the Windows update triggers a recovery, the key hasn't been escrowed to Intune yet (race). Can you boot to the WinRE command prompt from the recovery screen and run `manage-bde -protectors -get c:` to show what protectors are present?
Priya: I can try. here's the output I copied via the recovery command prompt:```powershell
C:\> manage-bde -protectors -get c:
BitLocker Drive Encryption: Configuration Tool version 10.0.19041
Volume C: [OS]
[Numerical Password]
  ID: {1111-2222-3333-4444}
  Password:
    012345-REDACTED-RECOVERY-CODE-0000
TPM:
  Not Present or Disabled
```
Priya: it says TPM not present or disabled — laptop definitely has TPM (firmware says TPM 2.0).
ben-windows-it: ok that explains a lot. during OOBE the TPM may not have been taken ownership or was cleared during an update. We need to get the TPM taken ownership and have BitLocker re-protect so Intune can escrow the key. Two options: 1) we remote you a bootable USB with the WinPE provisioning image and a script to take TPM ownership and re-enable BitLocker (requires temporary admin recovery flow), or 2) we swap the device quickly. Which do you prefer?
Priya: I'd prefer the remote USB option so I don't lose time. I can meet IT at the lobby to plug in.
alex-sec: from security side, we only allow option 1 if an IT admin performs the TPM take-ownership step or we run a signed automation with an approved token. We will ensure the private recovery key is escrowed to Intune and logged.
sam-people: I'll coordinate pickup area and ensure you have badge access for the swap window.
ben-windows-it: OK I'll prepare a signed WinPE USB image and an approved provisioning script. It will do: clear TPM if needed, take ownership, enable TPM PCRs, run `manage-bde -on c: -rp` to generate a new recovery password and attempt to escrow to Intune via the device sync. I'll open ticket #ONB-5017 and assign two-person verification for the key escrow.
intune-bot: Action queued: device sync + request key escrow. Ticket ONB-5017 created.
Priya: thanks — what should I expect during the boot step? any prompts?
ben-windows-it: you'll boot to the USB, the script will run automatically and show a progress screen. It may ask to confirm clearing TPM (if previously owned) — we'll be on a Zoom while you confirm. After provisioning completes we'll force an MDM sync from Settings -> Accounts -> Access work or school -> Sync. Then Intune should show a recovery key.
Priya: great — I'm available after lunch. please ping me the slot.
ben-windows-it: booked a 13:30 slot. bring laptop + power, we'll meet in 3rd floor lobby. I'll DM the Zoom link.
alex-sec: once done verify with `manage-bde -protectors -get c:` and with Intune UI we will check "Recovery keys available: 1" before you leave. Also re-enroll your 2FA devices for device login if needed.
Priya: will do. thanks for the quick turnaround.
ben-windows-it: np. filing a short how-to for future provisioning to avoid TPM non-ownership race during OOBE. :memo:
